home.description: What time is it now and what's today's date? See your live local time, the date, the week number and the time in cities around the world on one page.

faq.q: How is the time on this site calculated?
faq.a: The time is synchronised with the site's server, so it is right even if your device clock is wrong. The time zone is read from your device settings. Synchronisation sends only a few small requests to the server and no personal data.

faq.q: Does Türkiye use daylight saving time?
faq.a: No. Since 2016 Türkiye has used UTC+3 all year round, and clocks are not moved forward or back. Many European countries still change their clocks, so their time difference from Türkiye can shift by one hour during the year.

faq.q: How is the week number calculated?
faq.a: Under ISO 8601, weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week that contains the first Thursday of the year. For this reason the first and last days of a year can belong to a week of the neighbouring year.

faq.q: How is the time difference between cities worked out?
faq.a: Each city's current UTC offset comes from your browser's time zone database (IANA), and daylight saving changes are applied automatically. "Ahead of you" and "behind you" always refer to your own time zone.

faq.q: How do I change the clock style?
faq.a: Swipe left or right on the clock; on a computer use the dots below it or the arrow keys on your keyboard. The styles include classic and minimal analogue, digital, analogue and digital together, versions with or without the date, clocks with a monthly calendar, a flip clock, a clock in words, a ring clock and a big date. Your choice is remembered on this device.

faq.q: How do I see the clock full screen?
faq.a: Press the full screen button under the clock. To leave, press the same button or the Esc key. You can keep swiping between styles in full screen too.

faq.q: Does the clock work independently of my device clock?
faq.a: Yes. The time is synchronised with the site's server, so it shows the correct time even if your device clock is wrong, and it tells you how far your device clock is off. The time zone is still read from your device settings.

faq.q: Where can I see Turkish public holidays and Ramadan?
faq.a: The yearly calendar page shows public holidays, bayram and eve days, kandil nights and the month of Ramadan on one calendar. The "Upcoming days" section at the top of the calendar page tells you how many days are left until the next holiday.

privacy.title: Privacy and Cookie Policy | Saat Tarih
privacy.description: What data Saat Tarih processes, how cookies and local storage are used, Umami statistics, the email list and your rights under Turkish data protection law (KVKK).
privacy.lead: This page explains which data is processed when you use Saat Tarih, why, and what your rights are. The site only collects what it needs; there are no accounts or ads and no cookies are set; statistics and external services only run with your permission.

p: The data controller is Bumba Teknoloji Limited Şirketi (Ataşehir / Istanbul, Türkiye). For any question or data protection request: [bilgi@bumbagroup.com](mailto:bilgi@bumbagroup.com).

ul: **Time and date:** Your device's time and time zone are read and calculated only in your browser. They are not sent to a server or stored.

**Location (prayer times):** If you press "Use my location" on the prayer times page, your browser uses your location only on your device to calculate the times. The coordinates are not sent to the server or included in statistics; your last choice stays in your browser's local storage.

**Weather (external service, with permission):** If you have allowed external services in the cookie preferences, the weather page and the clock styles with weather send the approximate coordinates of the province or location you chose (to about 1 km) straight from your browser to Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com), which provides the data; your IP address also reaches Open-Meteo. Without permission no request is made and a short note is shown instead. The Saat Tarih server does not see or store these coordinates; Open-Meteo's own privacy terms apply.

**Map (globe, external service, with permission):** If you have allowed external services in the cookie preferences and you zoom the globe on the home page beyond a certain level, map tiles are downloaded straight to your browser from OpenStreetMap's server (tile.openstreetmap.org); your IP address and the tile addresses of the area you are looking at then reach the OpenStreetMap Foundation. Without permission, or while the globe is zoomed out, this request is not made. The Saat Tarih server does not see them; OpenStreetMap's own privacy terms apply.

**Qibla and nearby mosques:** The qibla direction, distance and qibla time are calculated in your browser. For the compass, your phone's orientation sensor is read only in the browser (iPhone asks for permission) and is never sent anywhere. If you tap "Show mosques" and have allowed external services, the selected place's coordinates rounded to two decimals (about 1 km) are sent from your browser to the Overpass service (overpass-api.de), which serves OpenStreetMap data; your IP address also reaches this service. The Saat Tarih server does not see these coordinates.

**Alarm music (YouTube, external service, with permission):** If you add a YouTube link to an alarm in the alarm tool and have allowed external services, when the alarm rings the video is loaded into your browser with YouTube's privacy-enhanced player (youtube-nocookie.com); your IP address and the video's ID then reach Google (YouTube), and the player may store its own data in your browser. The link stays only in this browser, with your alarm. Without permission the player is not loaded and the alarm rings with its own sound. The Saat Tarih server does not see these; YouTube's (Google's) own privacy terms apply.

**Meeting poll:** The poll's title, candidate times, the names of the organizer and participants and their replies are kept in the part of the link after the # sign; browsers don't send that part to the server, so the Saat Tarih server and statistics don't see them. Whoever you share the link with (by message or email) can see it. The polls and replies you see are kept only in this browser, under the sth-polls key.

**Email list form:** The email address you enter, the consent you give with the "I agree" button in the window that opens, the selected language and the page of the form are processed by Bumba Group's shared list service (bumbagroup.com). Sign-up uses double opt-in: you are not added until you click the link in the confirmation email, and every email contains a one-click unsubscribe link. See the [shared privacy notice](https://bumbagroup.com/liste/aydinlatma?dil=en) for details.

**Server logs:** The server that hosts the site keeps a standard access log for each request, with the IP address, browser information, the requested page and the time. These logs are used only for security and troubleshooting, not to build profiles of people.

**Visit statistics (Umami, with permission):** Only if you allow statistics in the cookie banner or the cookie preferences, Umami, which runs on our own server, counts page views and these actions: language and theme change, whether a search found a result, joining the list, choosing a clock style, full screen, the first use of a tool, the type of location choice (province or location), and opening or downloading the Ramadan timetable. While doing so Umami processes your browser, operating system and device type, language, screen size, the address of the page you came from, and the country and city derived from your IP address; the IP address itself is not stored. Umami does not use cookies, but it links visits to a pseudonymous session, so it is not anonymous. The words you type in search, your email address and your location are not sent. You can withdraw permission at any time with the "Cookie preferences" link in the settings menu; Umami stops from the next page on.

**Time synchronisation:** To show the time independently of your device clock, your browser sends a few small requests to the site's own server and reads the date header of the reply. These requests only appear in the server's standard access log; nothing extra is sent.

p: The Saat Tarih iPhone and iPad app follows the same principles: no account, no ads, no tracking and no analytics. Data handled in the app:
ul: **Location:** If you tap "Use my location", your location is used on your phone to calculate prayer times and find the nearest province; an approximate location (about 1 km) is stored only on your phone. The "Automatic" option in widgets also uses your location only on your phone.

**Weather:** Weather in the app comes from Apple Weather (WeatherKit); for this, the approximate coordinates of the selected province or your location are sent to Apple. We never see this data; Apple's privacy terms apply.
**Map:** The globe in the world clock is shown with Apple Maps; map imagery is downloaded from Apple.

**Calendar:** Only if you allow it, events from the calendars on your phone are shown in the app; they are read on your phone and never sent anywhere. Adding and deleting events happens through the iPhone's own calendar screen and only with your confirmation.

**Notifications and alarms:** Prayer time notifications; special day, start of season, moon phase, sunrise and sunset, morning weather summary, on-the-hour and daylight saving notifications (each on by default except on-the-hour; can be changed in Settings › Notifications); alarms and timers are scheduled on your phone without any server. Only the weather summary asks the weather service (see the weather item above). The list is kept current with iOS background refresh; spoken announcements are generated on your phone.
**Email list:** If you join the list from the About page, your email address is sent to the shared Bumba list exactly like the website form; the email list notes apply to the app as well.

**Badges:** Achievement badges and your progress (badges earned and the day, clock models seen, the number of consecutive days of use) are stored only on your phone and never sent anywhere; you can delete them at any time with "Delete badges" in Tools › Badges.

**Interval workout:** While an interval workout you started is running, the app uses iOS background audio so it can announce phase changes with the screen locked; the voice is generated on your phone and no data is sent anywhere.

**Photos:** A photo you pick for the full-screen clock or a countdown is taken through the iPhone photo picker (no access to your photo library is requested); a reduced copy is stored only on your phone and never sent anywhere. Photos you choose for the slideshow (up to 10) also stay on the phone. Prayer-time and countdown share cards and CSV files are made on the phone and sent only to the app you choose.
**Preferences:** Preferences such as the clock model, province and world clocks are stored only on your phone and are deleted when you delete the app.

**Qibla and nearby mosques:** The qibla direction is calculated on the phone; the compass uses the phone's orientation sensor (with location permission, location is also used on the phone for true north). On the "Nearby mosques" screen the search uses Apple Maps: the search word and the area centre rounded to two decimals go to Apple; Apple's privacy terms apply.

**Apple Watch, Siri and the Lock Screen:** The Apple Watch app calculates prayer times on the watch; when "Place from iPhone" is selected, the selected place's name and coordinates are sent from the iPhone to the watch (Apple's WatchConnectivity) and nowhere else; if "My location" is selected on the watch, the location is used only on the watch. Siri and Shortcuts actions (timer, alarm, full-screen clock, next prayer, date) run on the phone; Apple processes voice requests. Live Activities on the Lock Screen (counters, next prayer) are created on the phone.

**Camera, sleep and focus:** To read the QR code or barcode of an alarm's dismiss task, the camera opens only while you save the code and while you turn the alarm off (permission is asked the first time); the image is processed on the device, not stored and not sent, and only the value read is kept on the device with the alarm. The shake and steps tasks use the motion sensor only while the task screen is open; steps are not recorded. Pomodoro history (day, minutes, task name) and the sleep schedule stay on the device; pomodoro noise and sleep sounds are generated on the device. Smart alarm: if you start a session on the Sleep screen, the motion sensor (accelerometer) is read during the alarm's smart alarm window and the alarm rings early when signs of light sleep appear; the motion data is kept only in memory and is not saved or sent. There is no sleep tracking (sleep stages, recordings) and the microphone is not used.

**Worship:** Your Quran bookmark, text size, dhikr counts, prayer and fasting tracker (prayed times, make-up counts, fasted days) and the amounts you enter in the zakat calculator stay only on the device; they are not sent anywhere and are not used for statistics or badges. The Quran text and prayers are bundled in the app. When you tap the link to the Diyanet translation site, that site opens in your browser. You type the gold price for zakat yourself; the app does not fetch prices.

**iCloud sync:** If "Sync with iCloud" in Settings is on (the default), settings, world clocks, countdowns, saved places, pomodoro and sleep records and worship records are synced through Apple's iCloud key-value storage with the iPhone, iPad and Mac signed in to the same Apple Account. This data stays in your iCloud account under Apple's terms; we cannot access it and it never reaches our servers. Location, alarms, running timers, notification settings, badges and photos are not synced. Turning the switch off stops syncing on that device.

**Health, morning journal, alarm photo and floating clock:** If you turn on "Save to Apple Health", each finished interval workout is written to the Health app as a workout (type, start, duration); the app does not read your health data and this data goes to no server. The morning journal (mood, sleep, intention, note) stays on your devices only (on the devices of your Apple Account if iCloud sync is on). For the photo alarm task the photo is not stored; only a tiny fingerprint (72 grey levels) is kept on the phone for comparison. Your calculation method, prayer-time alarms (iOS 26+) and Control Center buttons stay on the phone. The floating clock is a picture-in-picture window; it plays no sound and sends no data.

**Music alarms, location and calendar reminders, focus blocking, Mac, Apple TV and Vision Pro:** For an alarm sound, a 30-second part of the song you choose from your music library or Files is written to a sound file on the phone; the song is not sent anywhere (music library access is asked only when you choose). For location reminders, iPhone itself detects arrivals and departures; the reminder's place stays on the phone and the map comes from Apple. When you set an alarm for a calendar event, only that event's title and time are used. Focus blocking uses Apple's Screen Time framework; the apps and websites you choose are Apple's encrypted tokens and the app cannot see what they are. The Mac, Apple TV and Vision Pro apps calculate prayer times on the device; if you allow location, it is used only on the device to find the nearest province.

p: The Saat Tarih Android app follows the same principles: no account, no ads, no tracking and no analytics. Data handled in the app:
ul: **Location:** If you tap "Use my location", only approximate location permission is requested; your location is used on your phone to calculate prayer times and find the nearest province or district, and an approximate location (about 1 km) is stored only on your phone.

**Weather:** Weather in the app comes from Open-Meteo (open-meteo.com); for this, the coordinates of the selected place, rounded to two decimals (about 1 km), are sent to Open-Meteo, and your IP address reaches Open-Meteo's server with that request. For city weather on the spinning globe only those cities' coordinates are sent. Open-Meteo's privacy terms apply; we never see this data.
**Globe and map:** The spinning globe is drawn from an image inside the app; no map service is contacted.

**Calendar:** Calendar permission is requested only if you tap "Show my phone's calendars"; events are read on your phone and never sent anywhere. Events are added through your phone's own calendar app and deleted only with your confirmation.

**Notifications, alarms and interval workout:** Prayer time notifications and the other notification types (special days, start of season, moon phase, sunrise and sunset, morning weather summary, on the hour, daylight saving; each on by default except on-the-hour, changeable in Settings › Notifications), alarms and timers are scheduled on your phone without any server; exact alarm permission is used so they ring on time. While an interval workout you started is running, a foreground service shown in the notification announces phase changes with your phone's text-to-speech engine. Spoken announcements are generated on your phone.

**Photos:** A photo you pick for the full-screen clock or a countdown is taken through the Android photo picker (no gallery permission is requested); a reduced copy is stored only in the app's own files. Photos you choose for the slideshow (up to 10) also stay on the phone. Prayer-time and countdown share cards and CSV files are made on the phone and sent only to the app you choose.
**Email list:** If you join the list from the About page, your email address is sent to the shared Bumba list exactly like the website form; the email list notes apply to the app as well.

**Badges and preferences:** Badges and preferences such as the clock model, location and world clocks are stored only on your phone and are deleted when you delete the app. If Android backup is turned on on your phone, these records (and the copy of photos you picked) may be included in the device backup in your Google account; that backup is subject to Google's terms and we cannot access it.

**Qibla and nearby mosques:** The qibla direction and compass are calculated on the phone. On the "Nearby mosques" screen the coordinates rounded to two decimals (about 1 km) are sent to the Overpass service (overpass-api.de), which serves OpenStreetMap data; your IP address reaches this service. Tapping a mosque opens your maps app.

**Wear OS watch and shortcuts:** The Wear OS app calculates prayer times on the watch; if "My location" is selected, the approximate location is used only on the watch and sent nowhere. Timers and alarms that the Assistant or other apps set in Time & Date are stored only on the phone; the screen saver and running-counter notifications are created on the phone.

**Camera, sleep and focus:** The QR code or barcode of an alarm's dismiss task is read by Google's code scanner (Google Play services): the app does not ask for camera permission and never sees the image; only the value read is kept on the phone with the alarm. The shake and steps tasks use the accelerometer only while the alarm screen is open; steps are not recorded. Pomodoro history (day, minutes, task name) and the sleep schedule stay on the phone; pomodoro noise and sleep sounds are generated on the phone (a foreground service lets them play with the screen off, with "Stop sound" in the notification). Smart alarm: if you start a session on the Sleep screen, the motion sensor (accelerometer) is read during the alarm's smart alarm window and the alarm rings early when signs of light sleep appear; the motion data is kept only in memory and is not saved or sent. There is no sleep tracking (sleep stages, recordings) and the microphone is not used. The session runs as a foreground service (with "Stop" in the notification). If you add a Spotify or YouTube link to an alarm, the link opens in that app when the alarm rings; the app only opens the link and has no access to the music.

**Worship:** Your Quran bookmark, text size, dhikr counts, prayer and fasting tracker (prayed times, make-up counts, fasted days) and the amounts you enter in the zakat calculator stay only on the phone; they are not sent anywhere and are not used for statistics or badges. The Quran text and prayers are bundled in the app. When you tap the link to the Diyanet translation site, that site opens in your browser. You type the gold price for zakat yourself; the app does not fetch prices.

**Health, morning journal, alarm photo, silencing and floating clock:** If you turn on "Save to Health Connect", only the permission to write exercise is requested and each finished interval workout is written as an exercise session (type, start, duration); the app does not read your health data. The morning journal stays on the phone only (and in the phone's Google backup). For the photo alarm task the photo is taken with the phone's own camera (no camera permission is requested) and is not stored; only a tiny fingerprint is kept. Do Not Disturb access for "Silence at prayer time" is used only if you turn it on and grant it in the phone's settings. The floating clock uses the "Display over other apps" permission; it reads nothing on the screen and only draws the clock. Widgets and Quick Settings tiles use the app's own counters.

**Location and calendar reminders, focus blocking and Android TV:** If you add a location reminder, precise and "Allow all the time" location access is requested; Google Play services' geofencing detects arrivals and departures, the reminder's place stays on the phone and the app does not send your location anywhere. When you set an alarm for a calendar event, only that event's title and time are used. If you grant usage access for focus blocking, the app reads the name of the app in front once a second on the phone, only during pomodoro work time; this is not stored or sent. The Android TV screen uses the place selected in the app.

p: The Saat Tarih browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) never connects to the internet: the clock comes from your device, and prayer times and the Hijri date are calculated on your device from data inside the extension. Only your chosen province and the 24/12-hour setting are kept in the browser's extension storage and are deleted when you remove the extension. No statistics, ads or tracking.

Saat Tarih does not set any cookies. On your first visit a banner at the bottom of the page asks for your permission for visit statistics (Umami) and external services (Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap, YouTube); both stay off until you allow them. You can change your choice at any time with the "Cookie preferences" link in the settings menu. To remember your choices we use your browser's local storage (localStorage); these items are in the necessary group, stay on your device and are not sent to a server. You can delete them at any time in your browser settings. Bumba Group's shared cookie policy: [bumbagroup.com/cerez-politikasi](https://bumbagroup.com/cerez-politikasi?dil=en).

faq.q: Will I lose my time if I close the page?

faq.q: What is a lap and how do I record one?

faq.q: Which week of the year is it now?
faq.a: The live counter above shows today's week number. It follows ISO 8601: weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week that contains the first Thursday of the year.

faq.q: How many weeks are in a year?
faq.a: An ISO year has 52 or 53 weeks. It has 53 weeks when 1 January is a Thursday (or a Wednesday in a leap year). {year} has {weeks} weeks.

faq.q: Why is 1 January sometimes in the last week of the previous year?
faq.a: Under ISO rules, week 1 contains the first Thursday. If 1 January is a Friday, Saturday or Sunday it belongs to week 52 or 53 of the previous year, and some days at the end of December can belong to week 1 of the next year.

faq.q: What is the week number used for?
faq.a: Week numbers are not much used in daily life, but ISO week numbers are common in business planning, logistics, education and software. The tool on this page shows the week number of any date you pick.

tz.title: Does Türkiye Have Daylight Saving Time? UTC+3 Explained | Saat Tarih
tz.description: Does Türkiye observe daylight saving time? Türkiye has used UTC+3 all year round since 2016. Time differences and DST status for cities around the world.
tz.h1: Does Türkiye have daylight saving time?
tz.lead: No. Since 2016 Türkiye has used the UTC+3 time zone all year round; clocks are not moved forward or back in summer or winter. The zone is called Türkiye Time (TRT) and its IANA identifier is Europe/Istanbul.
facts: Clocks are not changed twice a year
history: Until 2016 Türkiye used UTC+2 in winter (Eastern European Time) and UTC+3 in summer (Eastern European Summer Time).
A 2016 decision made summer time permanent; Türkiye has stayed on UTC+3 all year round since then.

tz.note: The standard difference is the difference when daylight saving is not in effect. For cities that observe daylight saving it changes by one hour for part of the year; the "Right now" column shows today's actual difference.
tz.faqHeading: Frequently asked questions about the Türkiye time zone

faq.q: Does Türkiye observe daylight saving time?
faq.a: No. Türkiye made summer time permanent in 2016; UTC+3 is used all year and clocks are not moved forward or back.

faq.q: Which time zone is Türkiye in?
faq.a: Türkiye is in the UTC+3 time zone, known as Türkiye Time (TRT); its IANA identifier is Europe/Istanbul.

faq.q: Is the time difference with Europe the same all year?
faq.a: No. Many European countries observe daylight saving time, so their difference from Türkiye changes by one hour during the year. The table above shows today's difference.

faq.q: What does UTC+3 mean?
faq.a: UTC+3 means three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). When it is 12:00 UTC, it is 15:00 in Türkiye.

faq.q: How are the days between two dates calculated?
faq.a: You subtract the start date from the end date; the calculator does this automatically and also shows the result in weeks and in years, months and days.

faq.q: Do working days exclude public holidays?
faq.a: The working-day count leaves out weekends and Turkish public holidays; bayram eve half days count as 0.5 working days. Holiday data is the 2026–2031 data from our calendar pages.

faq.q: How is age calculated?
faq.a: The completed years, months and days from the date of birth to today are counted. The calculator also shows the total days lived and the days until the next birthday.

faq.q: How are prayer times calculated?
faq.a: The position of the sun during the day is calculated from your latitude and longitude. Fajr starts when the sun is 18° below the horizon, isha at 17° below, and asr when an object's shadow equals its length. The calculation runs in your browser.

faq.q: Is my location sent to the server?
faq.a: No. If you allow location access, the coordinates are used only on your device to calculate the times; they are not sent to the server or included in statistics events. Your last choice is kept only in your browser's local storage.

faq.q: Are the times the same as Diyanet's?
faq.a: The calculation is tuned to match Diyanet's times and differs by at most 1 minute at province centres. Official times are still the ones published by the Turkish Presidency of Religious Affairs.

faq.q: What are the iftar and suhoor times?
faq.a: Iftar is at the maghrib (evening adhan) time, and suhoor runs until fajr (imsak). In Ramadan you can check both in the monthly table.

faq.q: Can I use it abroad?
faq.a: Yes. The Use my location button calculates the times anywhere in the world. At very high latitudes the fajr or isha angle may not occur; then an approximate time is given with the one-seventh-of-the-night rule.

faq.q: What is the Hanafi Asr time and why is it different?
faq.a: Asr begins when the shadow of an object equals its own length plus its shadow at noon; Diyanet and the Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools use this. The Hanafi school waits until the shadow is twice the object's length, so Asr starts roughly 30 to 80 minutes later depending on the season. spring: Day and night are equal at the equinox, and over the following months the days lengthen quickly.
Flowers bloom and trees turn green; migratory birds return north.
Snow melts and rivers rise; the soil is made ready for sowing.
summer: The longest day of the year falls on the summer solstice.
The sea and the soil warm up, and the season for fruit and vegetables peaks.
Short nights and clear skies make this the best time to watch the Milky Way.
autumn: Day and night become equal again, and the days begin to shorten.
Leaves change colour and fall; birds such as storks and cranes migrate south.
It is harvest time: grapes, walnuts, hazelnuts and chestnuts are gathered.

Snow in the mountains stores the water for spring and summer.

why: Seasons are caused by the Earth's rotation axis being tilted by about 23.4° relative to its orbit around the Sun, not by its distance from the Sun.
When the axis leans toward the Sun, that hemisphere gets more direct light and longer days, and it is summer. When it leans away, it is winter.
At the equinoxes (around 20 March and 22 September) day and night are almost equal; at the solstices (around 21 June and 21 December) the day is the longest or the shortest.

faq.q: When do the seasons start?
faq.a: Astronomically, spring starts around 20 March, summer on 21 June, autumn on 22-23 September and winter on 21 December. The exact moments shift by a few hours from year to year; see the table above.

faq.q: What is the difference between astronomical and meteorological seasons?
faq.a: Astronomical seasons are based on the equinoxes and solstices, while meteorological seasons use whole calendar months (March to May is spring, for example). The latter makes climate records easier to keep.

faq.q: How does day length change?
faq.a: Day length grows from the winter solstice to the summer solstice and then shortens again. The change is fastest around the equinoxes, by a few minutes a day, and almost still at the solstices.

faq.q: How is the Moon's phase calculated?
faq.a: The phase comes from the time since the previous new moon as a fraction of the lunar cycle (about 29.5 days). New moon and full moon times are calculated with astronomical formulas to within a few minutes.

faq.q: What is the qibla time?

faq.q: Which way is the qibla from London?

faq.q: Why can a phone compass be wrong?

faq.q: Is there a difference between UTC and GMT?
faq.a: In everyday use both show the same time (UTC+0). UTC is the common time scale kept by atomic clocks; GMT is the time zone the UK and some other countries use in winter. The UK switches to BST (UTC+1) in summer, while UTC never changes.

faq.q: What time zone does Turkey use?
faq.a: Turkey has used UTC+3 all year since 2016 (TRT, Turkey Time) with no daylight saving time, so the difference with Europe is 1 hour in summer and 2 hours in winter.

faq.q: What is the nisab for zakat?
faq.a: According to Turkey's Presidency of Religious Affairs, the nisab is 80.18 g of gold or money and goods of the same value. Wealth that reaches it after basic needs and debts, and has been held for one lunar year, is subject to zakat.

faq.q: Why does the Hijri calendar move about 11 days each year?
faq.a: The Hijri calendar follows the phases of the Moon; 12 lunar months last about 354 days. That is about 11 days shorter than the Gregorian year, so Ramadan and the Eids come about 11 days earlier each year.

faq.q: Why do Hijri dates differ between countries?

faq.q: How do I add up hours and minutes?

faq.q: Is today included in the days left?
faq.a: No. The number of nights until the chosen date is shown: tomorrow is 1 day left. If the chosen day is today, it says “Today”.

faq.q: How are working days counted?
faq.a: Saturdays, Sundays and full-day public holidays in Turkey are excluded from the days after today; half days before the Eids count as half. Holiday data covers 2026–2031.

faq.a: Tabata is a 4-minute interval workout of 8 rounds: 20 seconds of very hard work and 10 seconds of rest. Pick it from the presets.

faq.q: Is there a rest after the last round?
faq.a: No. The workout ends when the last work period finishes; rest is only counted between rounds.

faq.q: What does 3+2 mean in chess?
faq.a: Each player has 3 minutes and 2 seconds are added after every move they make (Fischer increment).

faq.q: Who starts the chess clock?
faq.a: Under the rules, the player with the black pieces starts the clock, so White's time begins to run.

faq.q: What does BPM mean?
faq.a: BPM (beats per minute) is the number of beats in a minute. 60 BPM is one beat per second and 120 BPM is two.

faq.q: How does tap tempo work?
faq.a: Tap the button along with the beat at least twice; the average time between the last taps is turned into BPM.

faq.a: No. Browsers restrict sound from background pages; automatic speech only works while the page is open and the screen is on.

faq.q: Why is there no sound?
faq.a: The browser needs a voice for this language installed on the device. You can download voices in your phone's or computer's language and speech settings.

faq.q: Why do the sign boundaries shift a little each year?
faq.a: The moment the Sun moves into a new sign shifts by a few hours each year, so the change days vary between the 19th and the 23rd. On those days the birth time matters too.

faq.q: What is a Moon sign?
faq.a: It is the sign the Moon was in at the moment of birth. The Moon passes through a sign in about 2.5 days, so it may not be certain without the birth time.

faq.q: Which planets are visible tonight?
faq.a: The night sky page calculates when Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn are above the horizon in darkness tonight at the selected place, where to look and how bright they are. Venus and Jupiter are usually the brightest; Mercury stays close to the Sun and is only briefly visible in twilight.

faq.q: How far away is the Moon?
faq.a: The Moon is on average about 384,400 km from Earth. Because its orbit is an ellipse, the distance changes each month between roughly 356,500 km (perigee) and 406,700 km (apogee). The page shows the current distance and the next perigee and apogee.

faq.q: What is a supermoon?
faq.a: A supermoon is the popular name for a full moon that falls near perigee, the Moon's closest point to Earth. It looks about 14% larger and 30% brighter than a full moon at apogee; the difference is hard to notice with the naked eye.

faq.a: The list comes from Wikidata (open data, CC0): events whose exact day is known, foundings of states and international organizations, and birth and death days of famous people. For each day the entries with Wikipedia articles in the most languages are shown. The list is refreshed every year.

faq.q: Can I look at another day?
faq.a: Yes. Use the day picker on the On this day page to choose any day of the year, or step with the previous and next day buttons; the link in the address bar shows that day.

faq.a: From the announcements of the IANA tz database (tzdata), which operating systems and browsers use. Each item names the tzdata release that added it.

faq.a: Apple, Google and Microsoft ship new tz database releases with operating system updates. If you keep your device up to date, the time will be correct on its own.
